items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: I listened to Miles, I would listen to one record night after night after night after night... Herbie Hancock and Tony Williams and Wayne Shorter or George Coleman, and Miles and Ron Carter of course.

ctx.x: All this time were you listening to jazz music? You know, like let’s say Coltrane or the piano players? I’m thinking — I’m not sure how to phrase this, or even if it’s a question, but that was a goal also? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-

Yeah. Well of course yeah. I was heavily into Miles Davis especially. The Miles Davis of the sixties. I was very monolithic in my taste. I listened to Miles, I would listen to one record night after night after night after night. And in those days the old hi-fi, I had a stereo system with the two little speakers, and I put them in bed with me. And I would earmuff myself with the speakers. And if you lifted up the changer arm, you know the little handle at the top where you could stack records, if you lifted it up…
That’s really interesting you say that because I was sort of trying to phrase a question I’ve been asking recently this question that has to do with wrong notes when you’re improvising.
